cases.proves_bugs: BUG-244 MOVE, end-move (typed STRETCH) and CDSYNC branches only; the IL-text edit branch (the one
cases.title: A pipe between two open ends, saved high end first by Edit Pipe, stays downhill (no uphill record, arrow still turned) after MOVE, an end STRETCH and CDSYNC
cases.plan_item: Bug-proof plan wave 1 (BUG_PROOF_PLAN_31OCT.md), group P: relink after MOVE or an end move
cases.expected: A new 20 m pipe with open ends, 18.000 / 17.800, arrow rotation 0. CDEDIT typed 17.800 / 18.000 and Save: 'Pipe updated.', arrow rotation about 3.1416. After MOVE 0,1000, after STRETCH of the west end 1 m further west, and after CDSYNC ('CDSYNC complete.'), the arrow still reads about 3.1416, the Civil log holds no line 'Pipe inverts updated: <this pipe> from=17.' (the record never makes the low west end its From), exactly one IL 18.000 text is left, and Edit Pipe on the pipe shows 'The levels fall from point 2 to point 1; CE records that as the flow direction.' and never 'Upstream invert is lower than downstream'; Cancel closes it. No CE window is left open and the drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The record is rewritten by CE's relink when AutoCAD ends the native MOVE and STRETCH commands and by CDSYNC on the live drawing.
not_automated: The IL-text edit branch (edit the plan IL text 17.80 to 17.70, then grip-drag) is NOT driven: the IL texts are MText and the driver has no MText edit route; it goes to a Codex look. The real grip drag is replaced by a typed STRETCH of the end vertex.

The decisive check is an ABSENCE (no uphill record line). Its twin W244_BROKEN asks for that line and must FAIL; the twin cannot make CE write a real uphill line on the fixed build. The arrow and the status chip are sanity checks: in the old fault the arrow was also left alone, so they do not tell old from new.
